title: Global capture destination declarations
description: Bob capture drafts can declare one shared task or parent-task destination with @@ syntax, item-local markers override it reliably, and bob-cli plus Bob Mac Capture provide coherent parsing, completion, diagnostics, preview, notifications, and atomic writes.

notes.author: bob-cli-12.land
notes.text:
Verified both phases against the source, the commits, and live binaries; integrated and cleaned up.

PHASE VERIFICATION. bob-cli 9258da9 (12.1) and bob-mac-capture e40f891 (12.2) are the epic's only commits; both phase notes were addressed and neither phase left a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP. Reproduced both end-to-end acceptance examples from the plan byte-for-byte against temp vault fixtures: '@@foo' with a '@bar' override produced exactly three results across two notes with the header in neither, and '@@foo+a-id' inserted the first two captures as ordered sibling children of ^a-id with the authored detail still nested, an ordinary task in bar.md, and the fourth item under ^b-id. Confirmed inheritance precedence against every local marker family that landed before this epic: '@bar', '@bar+b-id', '@bar#Ideas', '@bar^new-id', '@bar+b-id#requirements' (the task-section grammar from 3d5c59b/8f95e87), and the bare '#' Pomodoro note (f171a7e/8ab074f) each win for their item while unmarked siblings inherit the header. Confirmed strict errors for header-only drafts, a second declaration, a declaration after content, extra tokens on the header line, '@@foo#Ideas'/'@@foo^id'/'@@foo:id', bad route chars, empty block ID, and --route/--task-ref conflicts; inline code still protects literal '@@'. Confirmed leading blanks, a blank line between header and first item, and CRLF all parse, and that a failing mixed batch (bad parent on item 3) left both fixtures byte-for-byte unchanged. Confirmed additive JSON: capture-parse emits global_destination with post-inheritance item routes and header-excluding indices, spans are global_route/global_sub_bullet_route/global_sub_bullet_block_id, diagnostics are ranged, capture success JSON adds an optional top-level global_destination, and UTF-8 byte offsets stay exact through non-ASCII bodies. Confirmed capture-complete parity between '@foo+'/'@@foo+' including --all-tasks missing-ID candidates, header replacement ranges that exclude both sigils, and inherited same-note wikilink completion routing to foo.md while a '@bar' override routes to bar.md.

CROSS-REPO SYNC. Diffed the bob-mac-capture fake-bob fixture's global parse responses against real bob output for '@@ma', '@@file+', '@@file+hand', '@@foo' task batches, mixed-override batches, and shared-parent batches: every span kind, range, mode, need, and item range matches exactly, so Swift is consuming the real contract rather than a drifted stub. bob-mac-capture CI run 32728276837 on macOS 26 is green for e40f891 (swift-format lint, build, and 332 tests, 0 failures), including all seven new global tests, so phase 12.2's locally-blocked 'just format-lint/build/test' is covered after all.

INTEGRATION. Nothing landed in bob-cli, bob-mac-capture, or bob-plugins between the epic's start (2026-08-24 11:57Z) and now other than the epic's own two commits; e40f891 sits directly on 29228d2 and its BlockIDFieldFocus tests still pass. bob-plugins only mirrors bob capture's indentation and Pomodoro-selection behavior and never parses the draft grammar, so it needs no @@ awareness; no script in bob-cli builds capture drafts. The one integration defect the epic itself introduced was cleanup I finished here: the draft-envelope refactor left split_capture_items and parse_capture_items_with_clip_control as thin wrappers with no production caller, kept alive only by #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]. Removed both and repointed their two unit tests at split_capture_draft and parse_capture_draft_with_clip_control.

VALIDATION. cargo fmt --check clean, cargo test green (642 lib + 374 cli + 27 + 31 + 1, 0 failures), cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features exits 0 with five warnings, all in dataview.rs/plugins.rs/projects.rs/task_status_hooks.rs and none from capture code.

FOLLOW-UPS. No phase proposed any. The one issue I found on my own -- those five pre-existing clippy warnings -- is a semantic duplicate of task bob-cli-v (Eliminate existing bob-cli clippy warnings), so I corroborated it with a +1 rather than filing a new task, noting that two of the five (chunks_exact_to_as_chunks in dataview.rs:2372 and task_status_hooks.rs:1402) appeared after that bead was written. No other follow-ups; no epic-symbol entries existed and this project has no just symvision recipe.

title: Free the @@ global destination from the header line and teach it to absorb
description: A `@@route` / `@@route+block-id` global destination declaration can be typed on any line of any capture item instead of only on a header line, and typing a bare `@@` inside an item that already carries a `@file` reference moves that reference onto the `@@` and deletes the original, so a draft can never end up with a shadowed local marker or two competing declarations.

notes.author: bob-cli-13.land
notes.text:
Verified all three phases against the plan and the source. grammar (5b15533): declaration tokens are recognized anywhere (confirmed a trailing @@foo on item 2 routes item 1 too, with global_destination.line reported), declaration-only lines still behave as headers, duplicate declarations error with both line numbers, shadowed declarations emit the global_destination_shadowed warning from both capture-parse and capture (warnings field + stderr), and GLOBAL_DESTINATION_EXTRA_TEXT_ERROR / MISPLACED_GLOBAL_DESTINATION_ERROR / GlobalHeaderLine / parse_global_header_strict / reject_embedded_global_declarations are all gone with no leftover 'header' wording in docs or --help. rewrite (025dc06): exercised bob capture-rewrite end to end -- absorb_local_marker for trailing, leading, child-line, and @cash+goog-exit markers; absorb_declaration deleting a whole declaration-only line; all four Rule A5 notices; Rule A6 no-op; idempotence; last-bare-@@ selection with sibling declaration deletion; cursor placement past the rewritten token. macapp (bob-mac-capture 0a31975): reviewed the panel trigger, staleness guard, notice announcement, and rewrite lane; rebuilt swift build --target CaptureCore and --target CaptureCoreTests cleanly (the app target and its tests remain macOS-CI-only on this Linux host). Full 'just' (fmt + clippy --all-targets --all-features + cargo test) passes on master.

Integration: no non-epic commits landed in bob-cli, bob-mac-capture, or bob-plugins between the epic's start (2026-08-24 15:01 EDT) and this landing, so there was nothing to merge back. Confirmed no other bob-cli module consumes the global-destination model (the remaining 'global' hits are Tasks-plugin global_filter) and that bob-plugins has no capture-grammar duplication. bob-cli-14 turned out to be a duplicate epic already closed as canceled against this one, so it created no conflict.

Follow-ups: bob-cli-13.2's PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP (the plan's Vocabulary section never classified the three-component @route+block-id#section form) is resolved in-epic -- the implementation's choice to treat it as a Rule A5 'cannot take a section' notice is correct, since @@route#Section is out of scope per Rule G5, and I documented that form explicitly in docs/capture.md and in 'bob capture-rewrite --help'. No other child proposed follow-ups. I also fixed one epic-caused defect found during verification: the capture-rewrite --help example 'bob capture-rewrite -f json -- "@@foo\\nBuy milk @@"' passed a literal backslash-n in any shell and produced a mangled single-line rewrite; it is now three printf-piped examples matching the convention capture/capture-parse already use, each verified to run. Considered and declined filing a task for a bare @@ typed alone on its own line not absorbing the preceding item's marker: that line is a declaration-only line owned by no item, so Rule A1 source 3 applies by design and capture-complete correctly falls back to route completion (context: 'route' with candidates), which is the intended behavior rather than a gap.

title: Reclaim disk space on / and /mnt/hercules
description: Both pressured filesystems return to a healthy steady state with durable headroom: `/` drops below 75% used and `/mnt/hercules` below 80% used, the backup system stops storing redundant full copies of regenerable build artifacts, and monitoring alerts before either filesystem fills again.

notes.author: bob-cli-15.land
notes.text:
Verified all seven phases against the live system, not just their notes.

## Phase verification (2026-08-26 ~10:20 EDT)

- **15.1 triage** — yearly-2/3/4 and monthly-2/3/4 gone from `/mnt/hercules/backup/home`;
  no dot-prefixed interrupted-rotation leftovers anywhere under `/mnt/hercules/backup`;
  `/mnt/hercules/plex` untouched; array at 528G avail (was 0).
- **15.2 rootreclaim** — APT archives 928K; journald 423.8M with `SystemMaxUse=500M` in
  `/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/90-bob-rootreclaim.conf`;
  `ARGS="--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d"` in `/etc/default/prometheus`;
  `snap get system refresh.retain` = 2; `/etc/tmpfiles.d/90-bob-var-tmp.conf` 30d rule with
  `/var/tmp` down to 6.7G; Docker build cache and local volumes both 0B.
- **15.3 plexthumbs** — `GenerateBIFBehavior="never"` in Preferences.xml, 0 `.bif` files
  remain under `Media/`, plexmediaserver active.
- **15.4 buildart** — `sase-core/target` absent; `~/.cargo/config.toml` sets
  `build.target-dir = "/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target"` and is genuinely in force (no repo-local
  `.cargo/config.toml` or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` override in the checkouts, and no file under a
  per-workspace `target/` has been written since the redirect).
- **15.5 bkexclude + 15.6 bklinkdest** — both landed in `~/Sync/bin/cron.jobs/backup.sh`:
  `--link-dest="${to}"` in `_backup()` plus most-recent-first cross-tier hints in the
  daily/weekly/monthly cron scripts, and the hardlink-corruption constraint documented in
  `_run_rsync()`. Proved `--link-dest` on the real array (ext4 on md0), not only a fixture:
  an unchanged file shared one inode with `links=2` across two rotations while a changed file
  got a fresh inode with the old rotation's content intact. Then caught the live 10:17 hourly
  run in flight and confirmed production hardlinking — `.aspell.en.prepl`, `gtd.log`,
  `.bash_logout`, `sos.yml`, `.NERDTreeBookmarks`, `.tig_history` each shared one inode with
  `links=2` between `home/.hourly` and `home/hourly`. That exactly inverts the defect the plan
  documented (`links=1`, distinct inodes for the same `.bashrc` across seven rotations).
- **15.7 guardrails** — five `athena.disk-space` rules loaded and evaluating
  (`AthenaHercules*` pending at 95.24% used); textfile collector exports both mountpoints;
  weekly cleanup functions present in `weekly_jobs`.

## Two defects this epic introduced, found and fixed while landing

1. **The disk alerts would have run on frozen data forever.** 15.7 wired the hourly metric
   refresh as a bare `prometheus_disk_space_textfile` in `cron.hourly/hourly_jobs`, but
   run-parts runs `/etc/cron.hourly` with cron's PATH (`/etc/crontab`), which excludes
   `~/Sync/bin/main` — confirmed exit 127 under that exact environment. All five alerts read
   `athena_filesystem_*_bytes` from that textfile, and node_exporter re-serves a stale textfile
   indefinitely, so the alerts would have evaluated the 10:02 values permanently. Fixed by
   calling the collector by absolute path (the same idiom `hourly_backup` uses to source
   `backup.sh`), with a comment explaining why. Re-verified with a real
   `run-parts --report --regex '^hourly_jobs$' /etc/cron.hourly` as root under cron's PATH and
   `cwd=/`: mtime and values advanced.
2. **The new backup excludes were deleting kernel modules and global npm packages from the
   `/usr` rotations.** 15.5 added `--exclude="**/target/"` and `--exclude="**/node_modules/"`
   to the shared `_run_rsync()`, which serves every backup job, not just `/home`. Combined with
   the pre-existing `--delete-excluded` that was actively removing
   `/usr/lib/modules/*/kernel/drivers/target`, `/usr/lib/modules/*/kernel/drivers/nvme/target`,
   `/usr/src/linux-headers-*/include/target`, and `/usr/local/lib/node_modules` (globally
   installed npm CLIs). The plan pre-authorized this branch: "Confirm with the user that no
   tracked, non-regenerable directory named `target` exists... If that is a concern, scope it
   to the known Rust crate roots." Such directories do exist, so I scoped both globs to Bryan's
   home tree (`bryan/**/target/`, `bryan/target/`, `bryan/**/node_modules/`,
   `bryan/node_modules/`) and re-sorted the exclude list. Verified against the live
   `_run_rsync()`: a `/home`-like tree still excludes every `target/` and `node_modules/` under
   `bryan`, while a `/usr`-like tree backs up `drivers/target/mod.ko` and `node_modules/sass/cli.js`
   again. The in-flight 10:17 rotation is running with the corrected list.

## Integration (step 2)

Nothing to integrate. No commit in the bob-cli repo mentions bob-cli-15, the newest commit
predates the epic (2026-08-25 16:20 vs. epic start 2026-08-26 08:19), and grepping the repo for
hercules / backup.sh / link-dest / cargo-target / node-exporter / disk-space returns nothing.
chezmoi manages 3867 files but none of the paths this epic touched, so no dotfile source needs
updating. This epic's surface is entirely host configuration.

## Goal status

`/` is at 54% used (400G avail), meeting the `<75%` target. `/mnt/hercules` is at 95% used
(528G avail) and does **not** yet meet `<80%`. That is structural, not unfinished work:
bkexclude and bklinkdest reclaim only as rotations cycle. Eleven `/home` rotations still hold a
`sase-core/target` copy (the audit measured one at 120G); monthly and yearly are already clean.
Hourly clears within ~1-2 days, daily ~5 days, weekly ~4-5 weeks.

I deliberately did not run the plan's optional accelerant (hand-deleting `target/` out of the
existing rotations). It is a multi-hour destructive pass over ~1-1.5T on an array that now has
528G of headroom and working alert rules, and it self-resolves as tiers cycle. bob-cli-1a is the
real risk to that timeline and is filed.

## Follow-up outcomes

- 15.2's gate-timeout proposal -> **bob-cli-17** (large, ready).
- 15.7's Alertmanager proposal -> **bob-cli-18** (medium, ready).
- 15.7's cargo target sweeper proposal -> **bob-cli-19** (small, ready).
- 15.4's live-workspace `target/` proposal -> **bob-cli-1b** (small, ready); re-measured at
  32.5G across 11 paths.
- New, found while landing -> **bob-cli-1a** (medium, ready): `_backup()` treats rsync's benign
  exit 24 ("some files vanished") as fatal and discards the completed rotation. 1931 occurrences
  in `/var/mail/root`, roughly two thirds of hourly runs. Pre-existing — failures appear well
  before this epic started — but it directly gates the `/mnt/hercules` drain above.
- **Declined:** 15.4's "periodic cargo-sweep-style job". Already implemented by 15.7 as
  `disk_guardrail_cargo_target_sweep` in `weekly_jobs`; only the missing binary remains, which
  bob-cli-19 covers. Filing it again would duplicate that task.
- **Declined:** 15.4's sccache evaluation. The shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` from the same phase
  already delivers the cross-checkout artifact reuse sccache was proposed for, and there is no
  measured remaining problem — `/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target` is 754M against a 229G volume.
  Recorded here rather than filed as speculative work.
- No semantic duplicates: searched all task statuses for gate/lock, alertmanager/prometheus,
  cargo-sweep/target, and rsync/backup/hercules terms, and swept every task bead created in the
  last week (one, bob-cli-11, unrelated). The only other in-progress epic, bob-cli-16 (Pomodoro
  bullet moves), has no causal link to any of these.

`sase bead epic-symbols bob-cli-15` reports no entries.

title: sase gate wait timeout leaves the gate pending and cancel_gate blocks on .response.lock
close_reason: Fixed by sase commit 00bb5a082, which bounded cancel_gate's .response.lock acquisition with CANCEL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and cites this bead's own source note.

notes.author: 0eq
notes.text: Stale-bead sweep 2026-08-27 (project owner asked for a review of every open task bead in sase and bob-cli). Verified against the sase repo at master eaf4ea891. src/sase/notification_gates/executor.py:61 now defines CANCEL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0 with the comment 'Bound on how long cancel_gate waits for .response.lock. An approved option command holds that lock for its full runtime, so an untimed wait here reproduces a cancellation that hangs behind it indefinitely (bead bob-cli-15.2 note #2)' -- naming the exact note this bead was filed from. cancel_gate (line 461) takes lock_timeout_seconds: float | None = CANCEL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and passes it to file_lock(bundle_path / '.response.lock', timeout=lock_timeout_seconds) at line 476. Commit 00bb5a082 ('fix(notification-gates): bound cancel_gate lock acquisition with a timeout') landed 2026-08-26 14:18 EDT, about four hours after this bead was filed. Since 'the gate is left in pending forever' was a consequence of that hang, both halves of the reported defect are addressed.

task_type_fields.location: sase gate wait/cancel path (`sase gate` wait timeout handling and `cancel_gate`'s `.response.lock` acquisition)
task_type_fields.repro:
## Repro

Observed twice while running epic phase bob-cli-15.2 (rootreclaim):

1. Create a confirmation gate via `/sase_gate` (e.g. `custom-2509bf01-2ff3-403e-9b25-ffd9846981da`).
2. Wait on it until the wait exceeds `gate_timeout_seconds`.
3. Interrupt the wait with Ctrl-C.

`cancel_gate` then blocks on `.response.lock` and never completes, so the gate is left
in `pending` forever rather than being cancelled. A second gate in the same phase

title: Hourly backup discards a completed rotation when rsync returns the benign exit 24
close_reason: Stale task bead swept from triage.

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

Roughly two thirds of hourly `/home` backups are thrown away, so the newest rotation is
routinely hours stale and the recovery point is much worse than the hourly schedule implies.

It also directly gates epic bob-cli-15's `/mnt/hercules` steady-state goal. That epic's
two structural fixes — the `bryan/**/target/` + `bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/`
excludes (bob-cli-15.5) and `--link-dest` hardlink rotations (bob-cli-15.6) — only reclaim
space *as rotations cycle*. Eleven `/home` rotations still hold a full
`bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase-core/target` copy (the audit measured one at 120G);
they age out only when their tier rotates. Every discarded run postpones the array's
drop from 95% used toward the epic's 80% target.

This defect predates epic bob-cli-15 (failures appear in `/var/mail/root` well before the
epic started on 2026-08-26 08:19 EDT). Filed by the bob-cli-15 land agent.
task_type_fields.location: `_backup()` rsync error handling in `/home/bryan/Sync/bin/cron.jobs/backup.sh` (the `if _run_rsync ... ; then ... else BACKUP_ERROR=$((BACKUP_ERROR | RSYNC_ERROR))` branch)
task_type_fields.repro:
## Repro

```bash
sudo grep -c 'hourly_backup exited with return code 16' /var/mail/root   # -> 1931
```

`_backup()` treats any non-zero rsync exit as fatal. rsync exit **24** is not a failure —
it means "some files vanished before they could be transferred", which happens on every
run because `/home/bryan/.sase/axe/lumberjacks/**/runs/*` and
`/home/bryan/.sase/agents_sync/cache/staging/*` are short-lived agent scratch files.

On exit 24 the script discards the freshly-completed rotation (`rm -rf "${_to}"`), skips
the atomic `mv` chain, and returns — so the rotation never advances even though rsync
copied everything that still existed.

Sample failure rate from `/var/mail/root` (only failures generate mail):

| Date       | Failed hourly runs |
| ---------- | ------------------ |
| Aug 24     | 13                 |
| Aug 25     | 20                 |
| Aug 26 (to 10:00) | 6           |

On 2026-08-26 only three hourly rotations landed (00:39, 05:39, 07:56) against six
failures. `/mnt/hercules/backup/home/hourly` was still stamped 07:56 at 10:15.

Fix: treat 24 (and arguably 23) as success, or at most as a warning that still commits
the rotation, while keeping genuine errors fatal. `--delete-excluded` is active, so a
committed rotation is still correct.

title: Carry a completed Pomodoro's name onto the follow-on placeholder in task-status-cycler
close_reason: Implemented in bob-plugins commit 926adc7 ('carry pomodoro names on completion'). buildPomodoroCompletionPlan parses the completed entry's name and constructs a new entry with formatPomodoroPlaceholderLine(createdPomodoroName); existing later Pomodoros remain untouched. The dedicated 'Pomodoro completion carries the closed Pomodoro name onto created entries' regression is present, and all 143 tests in scripts/test-task-status-cycler.cjs passed during this review. The product choice has already been made and shipped in source; no new completion-name implementation is needed.
description:
Proposed by epic bead bob-cli-16 (Pomodoro sub-bullet moves and named Pomodoros) at landing, from its plan's "Out of scope" section, which asked the land agent to file the item via /sase_new_task if it still looked worth doing.

Named Pomodoros (`- [ ] () — NAME`) exist as of bob-navigation-hotkeys 1.28.0, but `task-status-cycler`'s Ctrl+Enter completion path still creates the follow-on Pomodoro as a bare unnamed `- [ ] ()`, so a completed named Pomodoro's successor loses the name.

links.description: Epic bob-cli-16 added the named-Pomodoro grammar (parsePomodoroEntryLine / formatPomodoroEntryLine in bob-navigation-hotkeys) that this task should mirror, and deferred this item in its plan's Out of scope section.
Same file and plugin (plugins/task-status-cycler/main.js); a fix here touches the same Pomodoro completion helpers.
Both touch buildPomodoroCompletionPlan in task-status-cycler and could collide in the same release.
Both touch task-status-cycler Pomodoro completion helpers and could collide in the same release.

task_type_fields.proposal:
When `Ctrl+Enter` completes a named Pomodoro (`- [ ] (**0920-0950** [t:: 30m]) — VERIFY`), the follow-on placeholder that `buildPomodoroCompletionPlan` inserts should carry the same name forward: `- [ ] () — VERIFY`. Today it always inserts a bare `- [ ] ()`, so the name is silently dropped and an unfinished VERIFY session continues as an unnamed Pomodoro.

Precise root cause and change site: `plugins/task-status-cycler/main.js` in the `bob-plugins` repo. `buildPomodoroCompletionPlan` (~line 3284) pushes an `insertLines` edit whose first line is the module-level constant `POMODORO_PLACEHOLDER_LINE = "- [ ] ()"` (~line 66), unconditionally. The fix reads the completed entry line's optional ` — NAME` suffix and formats the inserted entry with it, mirroring `formatPomodoroEntryLine` / `parsePomodoroEntryLine` in `plugins/bob-navigation-hotkeys/main.js` (~lines 6451 and 6533), which epic bob-cli-16 added as the canonical named-Pomodoro grammar. Add coverage in `scripts/test-status-cycler*.cjs`, bump the `task-status-cycler` manifest, and run `bob plugins sync`.

Open design question for triage: inheriting the name is the reading this bead recommends (a session named VERIFY that runs out of time continues as VERIFY), but "a fresh Pomodoro is a fresh purpose, so leave it unnamed" is an equally coherent answer. If the project owner prefers the current behavior, close this bead as canceled rather than launching it.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic bob-cli-16 introduced named Pomodoros and the `<ctrl+shift+m>` bullet-move keymap in the `bob-navigation-hotkeys` plugin. Its plan (`202608/pomodoro_bullet_move.md`) listed this under "Out of scope" because the completion path lives in a different plugin (`task-status-cycler`) with its own manifest, tests, and sync, and because whether a follow-on Pomodoro should inherit its predecessor's name is a product decision rather than part of shipping the keymap. The epic's land agent verified the deferral still stands at close and filed this proposal.

their only off-machine copy. Epic bob-cli-1e proved that is not a safe place to
leave data: excluding a folder from Sync, or rebuilding the remote vault, drops
every remote-only file.

Breakdown by extension (2026-08-27, from the sync client's `server_files` state
DB diffed against `git -C ~/bob ls-files`):

| ext | files | size |
| --- | ----- | ---- |
| `.zot` | 22 | 0.01 MB |

Root cause: `~/bob/.gitignore` ignores `*` and re-includes a fixed extension

and `.pyc` is build output — so this needs a per-extension decision, not a
blanket `!*`.

`old_lib/gov/2024_tax_return.PDF`, whose uppercase `.PDF` extension fell through
the case-sensitive `!*.pdf` re-include (vault commit ac31423).

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
Add a sync-topology section covering the facts epic bob-cli-1e established:

- `ob-sync-bob.service` (systemd user unit) runs `~/.local/bin/ob-sync-bob-poll`,
  a bash loop that invokes `ob sync --path /home/bryan/bob` in a **fresh
  process** every 30 s with a 120 s timeout. Config is therefore re-read every
  cycle and no restart is needed to pick up a settings change.
- The poll service does **not** participate in the `ob::acquire_lock()` lock that
  `bob nightly` and `bob bulk-git-commit` share, so quiescing sync means both
  stopping the service *and* gating the 03:30 `bob nightly` crontab line.
- Device-local exclusions: the headless client stores `ignoreFolders` in
  `~/.config/obsidian-headless/sync/<vault-id>/config.json` (set via
  `ob sync-config --excluded-folders`, a whole-list replacement); desktop
  Obsidian stores its own list in `.obsidian/sync.json`, which is neither synced
  nor Git-tracked. The value is prefix-matched and case-sensitive, and it is
  currently `["old_lib"]` on athena.
- An exclusion never deletes already-synced remote data; deletions must be pushed
  before the exclusion is set. Cross-reference `docs/obsidian-sync-exclusions.md`
  in bob-cli.
- Obsidian Sync **Standard** limits: 1 GB total storage, 5 MB max file size, ~1
  month version history, 1 synced vault. Version history and attachments both
  count toward the 1 GB ceiling.
- The remote's own inventory is readable offline from the sync client's SQLite
  state DB at `~/.config/obsidian-headless/sync/<vault-id>/state.db`, table
  `server_files` (`data` is JSON with `path`, `size`, `folder`, `deleted`).

notes.author: bob-cli-1n.land
notes.text: Superseded by epic bob-cli-1n (retire phase, commit 4051bf5). The requested behavior is now unconditional rather than opt-in: src/native/nightly.rs no longer runs an 'ob sync' gate at all. Its STEPS list is vault-sync, move-done-tasks, vault-sync, and the run loop is documented and implemented as 'a failing step does not stop later steps' — every step runs and nightly exits with the first non-zero step code. The bulk-git-commit step this task wanted protected no longer exists; vault-sync is the durable off-machine commit path and it runs first and last. No --continue-on-sync-failure flag is needed. Verified by reading src/native/nightly.rs at 4c00ada. Closed by bob-cli-1n.land.

links.description: 1i is the sync outage that makes 1j's abort-on-gate-failure behavior bite; 1j closing would remove 1i's 'no automatic vault Git commits' impact.

task_type_fields.proposal:
Let `bob nightly` run its wrapped maintenance steps when the shared Obsidian
sync gate fails, instead of aborting the whole run.

`src/native/nightly.rs` runs `ob sync` as a gate and returns early on failure:

```rust
let sync_label = match run_sync_gate(&styler, &vault, &child_env) {
    Ok(label) => label,
    Err(code) => {
        print_abort_summary(&styler);
        return code;
    }
};
```

so neither `move-done-tasks` nor `bulk-git-commit` runs. The module doc states
this is deliberate ("A failure here aborts the whole run before any wrapped step
touches the vault"), and it is right for a transient sync error. It is wrong for
a multi-day outage: `bulk-git-commit` is the vault's only durable off-machine
backup path, and it has no dependency on sync succeeding.

Options worth weighing: a `--continue-on-sync-failure` flag; running
`bulk-git-commit` unconditionally while still gating `move-done-tasks` (which
does mutate notes and is the step the gate really protects); or failing the gate
only for errors that indicate the vault is mid-transfer, treating a quota
rejection as non-blocking.

Discovered while landing epic bob-cli-1e (Remove old_lib from Obsidian Sync and
restore the vault under quota).
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
Epic bob-cli-1e was scoped to removing `old_lib/` from Obsidian Sync and getting
the remote back under the 1 GB quota. Changing `bob nightly`'s failure semantics
is a behavior change to a different subsystem with real safety trade-offs — the
gate exists so wrapped steps never mutate a half-synced vault — so it needs its
own design decision rather than a drive-by edit during a landing.

It surfaced now because the epic's Q2 decision (wait for version history to
expire rather than rebuild the remote vault, tracked in bob-cli-1i) leaves sync
red for up to ~2 weeks, which turns a normally-invisible design choice into ~2
weeks with no automatic vault Git commits.

description:
Two vault attachments cannot be pushed to `git@github.com:bobs-org/bob.git`
because GitHub hard-rejects any push containing a file over 100 MiB
(104,857,600 bytes) and this repo does not use Git LFS:

| file | bytes | MiB |
| ---- | ----- | --- |
| `old_lib/docs/vim_help_netrw.pdf` | 145,418,448 | 138.7 |
| `old_lib/docs/nvim_help_lua_intro.pdf` | 143,194,353 | 136.6 |

They arrived on athena during the bob-cli-1e landing: they were part of the 40
MacBook-only `old_lib` files (all >5 MB, so Obsidian Sync Standard never uploaded
them) that were rsynced to athena per the user's Q3 decision. Vault commit
aedc9f5 tracks the other 38 (591 MB) and adds an explicit `.gitignore` stanza
excluding these two, so the push succeeds.

Current copies: `/home/bryan/bob/old_lib/docs/` (athena),
`/home/bryan/var/backups/bob-old-lib-20260827/docs/` (athena), and the MacBook.
That is three copies but only two machines and **zero off-site** — every other
vault file has GitHub as its off-site copy.

Also note two files that do push but exceed GitHub's 50 MiB warning threshold:
`old_lib/books/adtech_book.pdf` (86.5 MiB) and
`old_lib/blogs/goog_multi_agent_patterns.pdf` (56.2 MiB). The vault `.git` is now
~1.34 GB, past GitHub's 1 GB recommended size.

Remediation is a choice, not a mechanical fix: enable Git LFS for the vault repo,
push these two to a separate object store, or re-render them (145 MB for a Vim
help page is almost certainly an unoptimised print-to-PDF and may compress by an
order of magnitude).

links.description: Same durability concern from the other direction: 1g covers vault files Git ignores by extension, 1k covers vault files Git cannot hold at all. A single off-site-backup decision could resolve both.
The two old_lib PDFs over GitHub's 100 MiB limit are the hard edge of this policy question; the policy should subsume them or say they stay out of band.

title: Decide a PDF-tracking policy for the Bob vault Git repo
description:
Epic bob-cli-1n made the bobs-org/bob GitHub repo the Bob vault's only sync channel. Its decision D3 deliberately deferred a general PDF-tracking policy for the vault repo rather than attempt one mid-cutover, and the plan's Non-goals section names it explicitly: "A general PDF-tracking policy for the vault repo (follow-up, per D3)."

The vault repo now carries three inconsistent PDF regimes with no written rule reconciling them:

1. `lit_review/` (276 files, ~430 MB) is gitignored per D1 and is pure out-of-band storage. Nothing copies it between athena and the MacBook; the runbook just says "copy it explicitly when a second machine needs the PDFs."
2. `xlib/` is gitignored per D2 and bridged by rsync through the `bob highlights scan` pre-scan command.
3. `lib/**` PDFs stay on the git channel per D3: 113 PDFs on athena, ~66 MB untracked at plan time and 23 already tracked. They are the Highlights pipeline's inputs, their `.md` sidecars carry a `source_pdf_sha256` that must match, and Obsidian embeds them in `ref/` notes. D3 called this "a deliberate, bounded exception to 'no PDFs in the repo'."

Untracking the 23 already-tracked `lib/**` PDFs was rejected at plan time because it would delete them from the MacBook on its first pull. That constraint has not gone away, so this needs a real decision rather than a drive-by `.gitignore` edit.

Proposed by epic bob-cli-1n (decision D3 and the plan's Non-goals section), filed by bob-cli-1n.land.

links.description: The two old_lib PDFs over GitHub's 100 MiB limit are the hard edge of this policy question; the policy should subsume them or say they stay out of band.
bob-cli-1g is the non-PDF half of the same gap: 86 vault files fall through the same allowlist .gitignore this task must edit. Coordinate one rewrite, not two.

task_type_fields.proposal: Write down, and enforce in ~/bob/.gitignore, one policy that says which PDFs belong in the bobs-org/bob repo and which stay out of band. Cover at minimum: whether lib/** PDFs stay tracked as D3's bounded exception or move out of band; whether the ~66 MB of untracked lib/** PDFs should be added, given their .md sidecars carry a source_pdf_sha256 that must match; a size ceiling per file and in aggregate, since GitHub's hard limit is 100 MiB per file and bob vault-sync already refuses at 95 MiB and warns at 50 MiB; a migration path for the 23 already-tracked lib/** PDFs that does not delete them from the MacBook on its next pull; and how lit_review/ reaches a second machine now that nothing copies it automatically. Record the outcome in docs/vault-git-sync.md so the next agent does not have to re-derive it.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic bob-cli-1n's job was to replace Obsidian Sync with git without losing data. Decision D3 froze the PDF regimes exactly as it found them precisely so the cutover would not also be a data-migration, and the plan's Non-goals section names a general PDF-tracking policy as out of scope. Changing which PDFs are tracked is a deletion-and-migration decision across two real machines with a 1.19 GB repo, so it needs its own design pass rather than a mid-cutover edit.

title: Give the MacBook vault-sync trigger an fswatch watcher instead of a bare 15s StartInterval
close_reason: Retain the deliberate D9 Mac trigger choice. Launchd's 15-second StartInterval handles sleep/wake and missed intervals without a Homebrew fswatch dependency or resident watcher. This task is the conditional 'if the delay becomes annoying' follow-up, not a reported lost-sync or user latency incident. Its old CPU estimate is explicitly uncertain because only 25/300 samples caught a process, and it does not demonstrate that fswatch reduces total cost. Changing the trigger now would reverse an accepted operational tradeoff on a hypothesis. Reopen for a concrete latency complaint or a current sustained CPU/energy measurement that justifies the added watcher.
description:
Epic bob-cli-1n's decision D9 gave athena and the MacBook different vault-sync triggers on purpose:

- athena runs a systemd user service executing `~/bin/bob_vault_sync_watch`, a loop around `inotifywait -t 15`. One blocking wait returns on either a file event or the timeout, so athena gets edge-triggered push plus a 15-second poll floor from a single process.
- The MacBook runs the LaunchAgent `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.bbugyi.bob-vault-sync.plist` with `StartInterval 15` and **no watcher**, so every outbound change waits up to 15 seconds and each interval spawns a full `bob vault-sync -q` process.

D9 chose `StartInterval` over the research report's `fswatch`-under-`KeepAlive` recommendation because it needs no Homebrew dependency, has no resident process to leak, and launchd already handles sleep/wake and missed intervals natively. D9 closes with: "If a 15-second outbound delay from the MacBook ever becomes annoying, adding `fswatch` is a follow-up, not a redesign."

Related measurement: epic phase bob-cli-1n.6 recorded acceptance test #18 (idle CPU over 10 minutes) at a MacBook average of 1.875% against a stated ceiling of ~1.5% of one core, with 25 of 300 samples nonzero and a 142.7% peak. That profile is consistent with unconditional 15-second process spawns rather than a resident watcher, so an event-driven trigger may cut idle CPU as well as latency. Whoever takes this should coordinate with the remaining bob-cli-1n acceptance work on #18 rather than measuring twice.

Proposed by epic bob-cli-1n (decision D9), filed by bob-cli-1n.land.

notes.author: bob-cli-1n.land
notes.text: MEASUREMENT CORRECTION from bob-cli-1n.land. The description above suggests bob-cli-1n.6's sampled ps pcpu figures were the wrong methodology. That was too strong: summing pcpu snapshots at a uniform interval and dividing by the sample count is a valid Riemann approximation of CPU-seconds over wall-clock, and it cross-validates well. I independently measured athena's bob-vault-sync.service today with systemd cgroup accounting (CPUUsageNSec 12.97 CPU-seconds over 2431 wall-seconds of live operation) and got 0.533% of one core, against the 0.588% the phase agent obtained by sampling. The sampled numbers are trustworthy; their real weakness on the MacBook is small-sample error, because only 25 of 300 samples caught a running process, so the reported 1.875% carries meaningful uncertainty. Treat the Mac figure as a genuine modest overshoot of the ~1.5% target rather than a measurement artifact, and note it is already well under ob-sync-bob.service's measured 4% baseline. Prefer launchd/cgroup-style total-CPU-time accounting over a longer window when you re-measure, for precision rather than correctness.

task_type_fields.proposal: Replace or augment the MacBook's StartInterval-15 LaunchAgent with an event-driven fswatch watcher so vault edits made on the MacBook push immediately instead of waiting up to 15 seconds, and so idle CPU is not spent spawning bob vault-sync on an unconditional timer. Keep a timer floor as a backstop so a missed or dropped event cannot strand the vault, keep launchd's native sleep/wake handling, and ship the change through chezmoi like the rest of the MacBook trigger. Re-measure idle CPU afterward with total CPU-seconds over wall-clock, not sampled ps pcpu, and confirm acceptance test #18's ceiling is met.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Decision D9 in epic bob-cli-1n deliberately shipped the simpler StartInterval trigger first: it needs no Homebrew dependency, has no resident process to leak, and let the epic cut over without adding a new runtime dependency on the MacBook. D9 states outright that adding fswatch later is a follow-up rather than a redesign, because the sync policy lives in the Rust command and only the trigger differs per platform.

title: MacBook chezmoi apply fails in install_nvim because cmake is missing
close_reason: Stale task bead swept from triage.
description:
Discovered by epic phase bob-cli-1n.5 (Provision credentials, triggers, and the MacBook git clone) while shipping the chezmoi rsync bridge and Bob config to the MacBook. Recorded there as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1.

A broad `/opt/homebrew/bin/chezmoi apply` on the MacBook fails inside `.chezmoiscripts/install_nvim` because `cmake` is not installed. The phase worked around it by running targeted `chezmoi apply --include files` invocations instead of a full apply, which was enough to land that phase's files but leaves the MacBook unable to take a plain `chezmoi apply`.

The chezmoi dotfiles live in the `chezmoi` linked repo (see the athena project's CLAUDE.md); open it with `/sase_repo` before editing. Filed against bob-cli because that is where the epic that discovered it lives, matching the precedent set by bob-cli-1h.

Proposed by bob-cli-1n.5, filed by bob-cli-1n.land.

title: Linux swift test: two BobProcessClient termination tests fail while macOS CI passes
description:
Proposed by epic bob-cli-1t phase bead bob-cli-1t.5 (note #1) and confirmed by the
bob-cli-1t land agent.

Two `CaptureCoreTests` process-lifecycle tests fail deterministically on the Linux host
`athena` while the repository's `macOS 26 SwiftPM` CI job is green:

```
Tests/CaptureCoreTests/BobProcessClientTests.swift:827: error:
  BobProcessClientTests.testCancellationTerminatesProcess : XCTAssertTrue failed
Tests/CaptureCoreTests/BobProcessClientTests.swift:863: error:
  BobProcessClientTests.testRunTerminatesAndThrowsTimedOutWhenProcessOutlivesTheTimeout :
  XCTAssertTrue failed - Expected the timed-out process to be terminated, not left running
```

`swift test` on bob-mac-capture master (c9f2e9f) reports
`Executed 126 tests, with 2 failures` on Linux; GitHub Actions run 33196599944 for the
same SHA passes every job (lint, build, test, bundle, signature, launch smoke).

Both tests predate this epic: `testCancellationTerminatesProcess` and
`testRunTerminatesAndThrowsTimedOutWhenProcessOutlivesTheTimeout` were introduced by
9030832 / 88cc781, and c9f2e9f did not touch them. They were simply never observable
here, because `Package.swift` used to declare the AppKit `BobMacCapture` target
unconditionally and the whole package failed to build on Linux. c9f2e9f made
`BobMacCapture`/`BobMacCaptureTests` macOS-only, so Linux agents can now run
`swift test` — and these two failures are what that exposed.

Decide the right remedy and apply it:

- If `BobProcessClient` genuinely fails to terminate a timed-out or cancelled child
  process on Linux Foundation, fix the client.
- If the tests encode a macOS-only assumption about how `Process.terminate()` becomes
  observable, make them platform-conditional or relax the assertion.

Leaving them as-is costs every future Linux agent a red `swift test`, which is now the
only Swift signal available before a push.

notes.author: bob-cli-1u--code
notes.text: Reset the child signal mask during Foundation Process.launch (restoring the caller mask afterward); Linux Swift concurrency had SIGTERM blocked in the spawned child. Moved the cancellation marker assertion before awaiting the task so it verifies signal handling within the fixture's delay. The two targeted lifecycle tests pass, and full Linux swift test passes all 206 tests. No fresh macOS run was available on this Linux host; existing macOS CI behavior was not rechecked.

title: sase stitch writes a wrong SASE_PLAN trailer when the bead's plan is machine-local
close_reason: Stale task bead swept from triage.
description:
Found by the bob-cli-1t land agent while verifying the epic's commits.

Every commit produced for epic bob-cli-1t carries a `SASE_PLAN` trailer naming the wrong
plan — `202608/highlights_annotation_tasks_section.md`, which belongs to the *previous*
epic — instead of the epic's own `202608/capture_named_pomodoro.md`:

```
$ git log -4 --format='%h %s%n%b' | grep -E '^SASE_PLAN|^[0-9a-f]{7} '
50a69c3 feat(capture): complete pomodoro-name completions
SASE_PLAN=[202608/highlights_annotation_tasks_section.md][2]
a03bd58 feat(capture): add bob capture-pomodoro-name write command
SASE_PLAN=[202608/highlights_annotation_tasks_section.md][2]
9b7282d feat(capture): add @route:id#pomodoro named targeting
SASE_PLAN=[202608/highlights_annotation_tasks_section.md][2]
cc4c9a3 feat(capture): list pomodoro ledger entries
SASE_PLAN=[202608/highlights_annotation_tasks_section.md][2]
```

The fifth commit, c9f2e9f in the linked `bob-mac-capture` repo, has the same wrong
trailer. Each trailer renders a markdown link to
`https://github.com/bobs-org/bob-cli--plans/blob/main/202608/highlights_annotation_tasks_section.md`,
so anyone following a bob-cli-1t commit's plan link lands on an unrelated epic's plan.
`sase bead show bob-cli-1t` resolves the correct plan, so the bead link and the commit
trailer disagree.

Likely root cause: this epic's plan exists only in the machine-local store —
`sase plan show 202608/capture_named_pomodoro.md` reports `source: local`, and
`git -C sase/repos/plans ls-tree --name-only origin/main 202608/` lists only
`highlights_annotation_tasks_section.md`. `sase stitch create` has no `--plan` flag, so
the trailer is derived automatically; when the bead's plan is absent from the SDD plans
store the derivation appears to fall back to some other plan in that store rather than
failing or omitting the trailer. Earlier commits whose plans *are* in the store
(9b534e3 → `block_scheduled_captures.md`, 86a0829 →
`resolve_archived_task_status_references.md`) got correct trailers, which is consistent
with that theory.

Fix should decide between: publishing machine-local plans into the project's plans store
when an epic launches; deriving the trailer from the bead's linked plan instead of the
store; or omitting `SASE_PLAN` when the plan cannot be resolved. A silently wrong link
is the one outcome to rule out.

title: Document that agents must watch bob-mac-capture CI after every push
description:
## Evidence

`plan:202609/fix_bob_mac_capture_ci.md` diagnosed five consecutive red `master` runs after `871eaed` (through `e5d7306` / run `34154292497`). Every run died in job `macOS 26 SwiftPM` step `Test`. Linux `swift build` stayed green because it never compiles those targets, so commits landed unwatched.

This implementation family then needed three CI iterations after the first compile fix, none of which a Linux host could have caught:

1. `33b89be` — file-scope fixture hoist; CI run `34163055815` still failed to compile because `XCTestCase.record` shadowed the helper.
2. `ef4611d` — rename to `applicationRecord`; CI run `34163503387` compiled 425 tests, then two `InstallRelauncherTests` failed because `URL.resolvingSymlinksInPath` does not equate `/var` and `/private/var` when later components are missing.
3. `cf73955` — fold `/private/{var,tmp,etc}` after resolution; CI run `34163916512` on `master` is green: https://github.com/bobs-org/bob-mac-capture/actions/runs/34163916512 (SHA `cf739555728f9915a80daeffbe2c04634b1fea3f`). Every required step succeeded, including `Install and reinstall`.

Current `sase.md` only describes capture-contract coordination for `bob-mac-capture`. It does not tell agents that the macOS-only targets have no local gate.

Related but not a duplicate: `bob-cli-1u` is a Linux `swift test` failure in CaptureCore while macOS CI is green — the inverse platform gap.

links.description: Linux CaptureCore test gap is the inverse of this macOS-only CI-watch convention

plus_one_evidence.note: Independent reproduction from bob-cli-2v.land (proposed by bob-cli-2v.3 note #2 and bob-cli-2v.5 notes #1-#2): bob-mac-capture commit e9865e6 (task-link picker, epic bob-cli-2v) was pushed to master without watching CI; run 36758703183 (macOS 26 SwiftPM) failed at step Test with a test-target compile error (TaskLinkPickerPresentationTests.swift:488/494, 'CapturePickerPresentation' has no member 'pullForwardLine'), so none of the new Swift tests ever ran. Both phases verified only 'just format-lint' and 'just build' over ssh on the mac tailnet host, whose Command Line Tools-only toolchain has no XCTest ('no such module XCTest' for every test target, identical on the clean base tree), and treated the red 'just test' as environmental instead of watching Actions. New fact for the memory update: the 'mac' tailnet host is not a test gate either, not just Linux. Impact: a red master was left behind and discovered only by the epic land agent.

task_type_fields.proposed_change: In the Repositories section, expand the `bob-mac-capture` linked-repo bullet so agents always see that GitHub Actions is the only type-check/test gate for the macOS-only targets. After any push to `bobs-org/bob-mac-capture`, they must watch CI to completion with `gh run watch --repo bobs-org/bob-mac-capture --exit-status` (via `/sase_monitor`) and keep iterating until a full run is green. Spell out that Linux `swift build` / `swift test` only confirm CaptureCore, because `BobMacCapture`, `BobMacCaptureInstallHelper`, and their tests are gated by `#if os(macOS)` and `Scripts/xcode-swift.sh` will not run without Apple developer tools.

Instead apply_plan succeeds and writes the file. Likely root cause: this sandbox's temp-dir filesystem (under /home/bryan/.cache/sase/tmp/...) immediately reuses the same inode number for a delete+create in the same directory, so FileIdentity's ino comparison in task_status_hooks_write.rs sees no change and the conflict goes undetected. Discovered while implementing the task-status-hooks retry-timeout plan (sase/repos/plans/202609/task_status_hooks_retries.md) running 'just all'; unrelated to that feature. Needs investigation into whether the test should assert something filesystem-portable (e.g. force distinct inodes, or detect+skip on filesystems with fast inode reuse) or whether this points at a real robustness gap in the preflight identity check on such filesystems.

(-n/--no-hooks) registered on the root command, inside with_scan_args in alphabetical position, and
directly on doctor — deliberately not on with_config_args, so marker/create/sync stay clean;
no_hooks_flag() ORs root and subcommand matches and threads into scan_library and doctor_vault, which
prints "pre_scan_hook: skipped (--no-hooks)" without recording a failure. Docs match the code:
README.md, docs/highlights-ref-sync.md, docs/vault-git-sync.md all carry -n|--no-hooks, pre_scan_hook,
BOB_HIGHLIGHTS_PRE_SCAN_HOOK, and the exported marker. Grep confirms every surviving occurrence of the
legacy spelling is an intentional rejection path or its doc/test.

PHASE 23.2 (chezmoi 475626a5, bob-cli 92042e9) — CONFIRMED in the linked chezmoi checkout.
home/dot_config/bob/config.yml renamed to highlights.pre_scan_hook; maybe_bob_highlights_sync renames
pre_scan_hook_configured, reads BOB_HIGHLIGHTS_PRE_SCAN_HOOK with the same set-but-empty semantics, and
awk-matches pre_scan_hook:. bob_xlib_pull gained run_scan() after both handle_host calls: returns early
on BOB_HIGHLIGHTS_IN_PRE_SCAN_HOOK, then takes the shared maybe_bob_highlights_sync.lock and returns
early if held, resolves bob via command -v then $HOME/.cargo/bin/bob (exit 1 + stderr if missing), runs
it through run_waited so the existing child-tracking and signal handling apply, and reports a non-zero
scan as exit 1. I traced the lock release: scan_lock_held is set only by the process that created the
lock and cleanup() rmdirs it, and cleanup is reached on normal exit via `trap 'cleanup' 0` as well as
through on_signal for 1/2/3/15 — so the lock cannot leak either way. Both scripts carry the shared-lock
comment. docs/vault-git-sync.md describes the auto-scan, both skip conditions, and the cron fallback.

checkout (`sase repo open` reports the primary workspace directory absent), matching the plan's non-goal.

EPIC-CAUSED ISSUE FOUND AND FIXED. While checking formatting I found the epic's own new test,
tests/cli.rs highlights_ref_scan_rejects_legacy_pre_scan_command_key, was written with a hand-wrapped
write_file(...) call that rustfmt collapses to one line under this repo's actual style. Fixed in this
landing and re-verified: zero rustfmt diffs tree-wide, and the highlights cli tests still pass.

FOLLOW-UPS. The child phases recorded no PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP entries (confirmed on 23, 23.1 and 23.2).
Two issues that I found myself and that this epic did not cause were routed through /sase_new_task:
 - Created bob-cli-24 (task(ci), small): `just fmt` fails repo-wide because bob-cli has no tracked
   rustfmt.toml, so cargo fmt falls back to max_width=100 and style_edition=2024 while the source is
   written at max_width=80 / style_edition=2021. Not caused by this epic — I reproduced 2529 diff hunks
   across 54 files on a clean worktree of the pre-epic commit 1d3373f, including files untouched for

   diffs. `just all` therefore dies on its first recipe; `just lint` and `just test` both pass, which is

 - Corroborated bob-cli-21 with `sase bead +1` (independent reproduction) rather than filing a

the new bob binary. In that order the worst case is a short window where an old bob ignores pre_scan_hook

title: just fmt fails repo-wide: bob-cli has no rustfmt.toml, so cargo fmt uses default max_width/style_edition
description:
`just fmt` (`cargo fmt --check`) fails across nearly the whole bob-cli tree, and has
done so since before epic bob-cli-23 started. On the epic's base commit `1d3373f` a
clean checkout produces **2529 diff hunks across 54 files**, including files no recent
work has touched (`src/lib.rs`, `src/runner.rs`, `src/native/ob.rs`, `src/native/nightly.rs`,
`tests/tasks_real_vault_parity.rs`, ...). `just lint` and `just test` pass, so `just all`
dies on its very first recipe and no agent can use it as a gate.

## Root cause (pinned by bisecting rustfmt config)

The repo has **no `rustfmt.toml`** — `git log --all -- rustfmt.toml .rustfmt.toml` is
empty, and there is none in any ancestor directory of either the canonical checkout
(`/home/bryan/projects/github/bobs-org/bob-cli`) or a SASE workspace clone. So
`cargo fmt` runs with stock defaults, while the committed source is formatted to a
different style. Two settings account for the entire gap:

| config | remaining `Diff in` hunks (tree-wide) |
| --- | --- |
| none (today) | 2529 |
| `max_width = 80` | 199 |
| `max_width = 80` + `style_edition = "2021"` | 0 |

- **`max_width`**: source is wrapped at 80, rustfmt's default is 100. This is ~92% of the noise.
- **`style_edition`**: `Cargo.toml` sets `edition = "2024"`, so rustfmt infers
  `style_edition = "2024"`, which reorders `use` braces case-insensitively
  (`{script_names, SCRIPT_ASSETS}` -> `{SCRIPT_ASSETS, ..., script_names}`), collapses
  short `if`/`else` to one line, and changes nested-macro indentation. The committed
  source predates that and matches `style_edition = "2021"`.

Earlier bead notes (bob-cli-1t.1, bob-cli-1y.3, bob-cli-1z.2, bob-cli-o) report
`cargo fmt --check` clean, so this regressed when the toolchain moved to an edition-2024-aware
rustfmt (currently `rustfmt 1.9.0-stable (59807616e1 2026-04-14)`, clippy reports rust 1.95.0).
Nothing pinned the style, so the style silently moved under the repo.

## Suggested fix

Commit a `rustfmt.toml` at the repo root. The owner should decide between:

1. **Pin today's style** — `max_width = 80` + `style_edition = "2021"`. Verified: zero
   diffs tree-wide, no source churn, restores `just all` immediately. Recommended.
2. **Adopt style edition 2024** — `max_width = 80` only, then run `cargo fmt --all` and
   commit the ~199-hunk reformat. Modernizes but produces a large, review-noisy diff.

Either way, `rustfmt.toml` must be tracked, since its absence is what lets the default
drift back in.

## Reproduction

```console
$ cd <bob-cli checkout>
$ git checkout 1d3373f
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check | grep -c '^Diff in'
2529
$ printf 'max_width = 80\nstyle_edition = "2021"\n' > rustfmt.toml
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check | grep -c '^Diff in'
0
```

Found by the bob-cli-23 land agent while running `just all`. The one formatting
deviation that epic *did* introduce (`tests/cli.rs`
`highlights_ref_scan_rejects_legacy_pre_scan_command_key`) was fixed inside bob-cli-23
and is not part of this task.

(a) After a failed commit, a rerun of a pending-only pull archives a block that was never committed. The epic plan sanctions this: pending-only pulls skip steps 4 and 6-8, and vault-sync commits the block later. (b) A target that is not valid UTF-8 is rewritten lossily. Obsidian notes are UTF-8, so this is effectively unreachable. (c) Verify locates a revision block's task line by its first exact match. The exactly-once whole-block check already guarantees the block is present. (d) Dimming the crash stderr tail is cosmetic; the text is already present. (e) The token-shape stderr warning under doctor -f json goes to stderr only, so the JSON is unaffected. (f) list -s vault silently falls back to the default target on an invalid config. This is intentional: -s vault needs no gkeep config. (g) Truncation drops the dim styling, emoji widths are off by one, the Keep-failure title shape differs, and human pull rows are not column-aligned. All cosmetic. (h) A leading 'N.' is escaped as '\N.' rather than 'N\.'. It renders a visible backslash but is safe. (i) The journal is not keyed by vault. There is one vault per host by design. (j) Glyphs appear in piped output: decided to keep always-on glyphs, because the epic plan pins those outputs and doctor rows need them; the unused ui helpers are deleted instead. (k) The login preflight does not resolve uv before consuming the cookie, and the exchange-auth hint mentions login. Both are minor; login fails fast with a clear setup error. title: Serialize the capture_pomodoros BOB_DAY_FILE test mutation
description:
`capture_pomodoros::tests::missing_note_and_missing_section_are_warning_successes` reads the process-global `BOB_DAY_FILE` while `tests::with_env` in the same module sets and clears that variable with no lock.

`capture_complete::tests` already documents the race and holds `DAY_FILE_LOCK` around every day-file override (`src/native/capture_complete.rs`, the static just above `day_file_guard`). That mutex is private to the module, so `capture_pomodoros` cannot take it. Lib tests share one process, so a `capture_complete` test can set `BOB_DAY_FILE` while the pomodoros missing-note test expects the default day file to be absent (or the reverse).

bob-cli-2c.1 proposed quarantining or serializing these env-mutating tests. The helper and the test predate this epic: both are from `cc4c9a38` (2026-08-28), "feat(capture): list pomodoro ledger entries". This landing did not catch a fresh fail-then-pass run; the defect is the unlocked mutation, which is visible in the two `with_env` implementations.

Share one process-wide lock (the private `DAY_FILE_LOCK` does not serialize across modules) or stop the pomodoros test from mutating the environment. Do not treat this as part of epic bob-cli-2c.

task_type_fields.impact: Parallel `cargo test --lib` can fail a warning-success assertion that has been in tree since 2026-08-28, or can hide a real missing-note failure by pointing the test at another test's day file. The start epic's own suite is unaffected when tests run serially.
task_type_fields.repro: Read `src/native/capture_pomodoros.rs` `tests::with_env` (sets `BOB_DAY_FILE` via `std::env::set_var` with no mutex) and `missing_note_and_missing_section_are_warning_successes`, which calls `list_capture_pomodoros` once with the ambient env and once inside `with_env`. Then read `src/native/capture_complete.rs` `tests::DAY_FILE_LOCK`: the comment says parallel tests must never set and read `BOB_DAY_FILE` at the same time, and `day_file_guard` is module-private. `rg BOB_DAY_FILE src/native/capture_complete.rs` shows many tests take that lock; the pomodoros test does not. A parallel `cargo test --lib` can therefore observe another test's day file during the missing-note assertion. This landing did not re-run that suite to time a failure.

creation_reason: bob-cli-2c.1 proposed serializing the capture_pomodoros BOB_DAY_FILE test mutation. The unlocked process-global write predates that epic and is not caused by the Pomodoro start work, so it is a separate bug.

task_type_fields.proposal:

title: Completed-reference relocation duplicates a Task Link already present in the destination completed Pomodoro

task_type_fields.impact: Minor but recurring ledger noise: every task completed while its link sits both in a finished session and in a carried placeholder can leave a duplicate (and unmarked) struck line in the completed session, which the user cleans up by hand; duplicate records also skew any per-session link counts.
task_type_fields.location: Completed-reference retirement/relocation: task-status-cycler Ctrl+Enter closed-reference retirement (bob-plugins) and its parity contract in bob task-status-hooks (src/native/task_status_hooks, docs/task-status-hooks.md 'Pomodoro Marker' relocation rules)
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed in the Bob vault's `2026/20260929.md` (vault git history):

1. Before: the completed `- [x] (**1350-1425** [t:: 35m]) — GTD` Pomodoro had child
   `🍅 [[bob#^pomodoro-ledger-daily-roadmap]]`, and the later open placeholder
   `- [ ] () — GTD` had child `[[bob#^pomodoro-ledger-daily-roadmap]]` (carried by the close).
2. At vault commit `8e502f3d` (2026-09-29 14:31:36 -0400, files: `bob.md` + the daily note)
   the task `^pomodoro-ledger-daily-roadmap` in `bob.md` was completed (`[x]`). This timestamp
   does not match the 15-minute `bob task-status-hooks` cron (:10/:25/:40/:55), so the writer
   was most likely the Obsidian Ctrl+Enter completion path (task-status-cycler's closed-reference
   retirement), though that is not confirmed.
3. Result in the same commit: the open placeholder's link was removed and the completed GTD
   Pomodoro now contained BOTH `~~[[bob#^pomodoro-ledger-daily-roadmap]]~~` and
   `🍅 ~~[[bob#^pomodoro-ledger-daily-roadmap]]~~`, i.e. the retired link was relocated into the
   last completed Pomodoro (the completed-fallback destination) even though that Pomodoro already
   held a link to the same task. The relocated copy also lacks the 🍅 marker that
   docs/task-status-hooks.md says a live non-transcluded link moved to the completed fallback
   should get.
4. At `0427125a` (18 s later) the user hand-deleted the unmarked duplicate.

Reproduce with `git -C ~/bob show 8e502f3d -- 2026/20260929.md`. To reproduce fresh: put
the same task link under a completed Pomodoro and under a later open untimed placeholder
(no open timed Pomodoro), then complete the task with Ctrl+Enter in Obsidian (and separately run
`bob task-status-hooks --dry-run`). Check whether the completed Pomodoro ends up with two
struck links to the same task.

title: gkeep_auth login_missing_email_is_a_setup_error panics with broken pipe writing stdin
description:
Proposed by phase bead bob-cli-2k.4 (Help and docs for =x<N>!<M>), triaged by bob-cli-2k.land.

`tests/gkeep_auth.rs::login_missing_email_is_a_setup_error` failed once during a full `cargo test` run with a broken-pipe panic. It passed on retry, both with and without the phase's docs-only changes. It passed in the bob-cli-2k.land full run on master b3405bd (gkeep_auth: 11 passed).

Likely root cause (from reading the code): `run_login` (tests/gkeep_auth.rs:99-122) spawns `bob gkeep login` with piped stdin, then calls `child.stdin.take().write_all(stdin_text).expect("write stdin")`. In this test `gkeep.email` is not configured, so login exits 2 with a setup error without ever reading stdin. When the child exits and closes its stdin before the test writes, `write_all` returns EPIPE and `expect("write stdin")` panics. This is a timing race.

Fix: make `run_login` tolerate `ErrorKind::BrokenPipe` on the stdin write (ignore it, then assert on the exit status and stderr as today), or write stdin from a helper thread and ignore the write result. Keep asserting exit code 2, the `gkeep.email` hint, and `fake.call_count() == 0`. Check the other stdin-writing helpers in tests/gkeep_*.rs for the same pattern.

task_type_fields.evidence: 1 failure (broken pipe panic at the stdin write) in one full cargo test run by bob-cli-2k.4; passed on retry with and without its docs-only changes. It passed again in the bob-cli-2k.land full run on master b3405bd. The failure is timing-dependent: the child exits on the missing gkeep.email setup error before the test writes stdin. Serial reproduction has not been attempted.

creation_reason: Phase bob-cli-2k.4 hit an intermittent broken-pipe panic in this test during a full cargo test run; the test helper writes stdin to a login process that can exit before reading it.

title: bob picks tomorrow's daily note after 8pm EDT on apollo (system TZ is Etc/UTC)
description:
Proposed by phase bead bob-cli-2o.13 (rollout of epic bob-cli-2o) and re-verified by bob-cli-2o.land.

Root cause: `bob_env::current_datetime()` (src/native/env.rs:90) falls back to `chrono::Local::now()` when `BOB_NOW`/`DATE` are unset, and `default_day_file()` (src/native/env.rs:113) derives today's `YYYY/YYYYMMDD.md` from it. apollo's system timezone is `Etc/UTC` (`/etc/localtime -> /usr/share/zoneinfo/Etc/UTC`, `TZ` unset), while Bryan's vault days follow US Eastern time. From 20:00 EDT (00:00 UTC) until midnight EDT, every bob command on apollo that picks "today" (`bob plan`, `bob capture`, `bob tmux-pomodoro`, `bob task-status-hooks`, `bob pomodoro`, notify) targets tomorrow's daily note, which usually does not exist yet.

Remediation options (pick one, or both):
1. Host fix: set apollo's timezone to America/New_York (`timedatectl set-timezone`, privileged; or `TZ` in the relevant user services and shell profile via chezmoi).
2. Code fix: let bob honor a configured vault timezone (e.g. a `timezone:` key in `~/.config/bob/config.yml`, falling back to the system zone) in `current_datetime()`, so behavior no longer depends on the host's zone.

task_type_fields.impact: Every evening after 20:00 EDT, captures, plan budget, tmux status, and task-status-hooks on apollo read or write the wrong (tomorrow) daily note or report an empty plan.
task_type_fields.repro: On apollo at 2026-09-29 22:31 EDT (2026-09-30 02:31 UTC), with BOB_NOW/DATE/BOB_DAY_FILE unset: `date` prints "Wed Sep 30 02:31 AM UTC 2026" and `bob plan` prints "bob plan - Wed 2026-09-30 - no daily note yet", while the live day note is ~/bob/2026/20260929.md.

creation_reason: Rollout phase bob-cli-2o.13 saw bob plan/capture target tomorrow's note in the evening; the land agent confirmed the host-timezone root cause, which is independent of the plan-budget epic.

notes.author: 3k
notes.text:
Closeout for epic bob-cli-2v (`:` Task Link Picker).

THE BUG AND ITS FIX: Bryan installed bob-cli f7d9c58 + bob-mac-capture e9865e6 and typed `:`: the panel showed "Pick any open task — press Tab to browse" but the picker card never opened. Root cause: a stdout pipe deadlock in BobProcessClient.run — it read stdout/stderr only inside process.terminationHandler, after exit. A pipe holds 64 KiB; capture-complete for `:` returns ~592 candidates / ~246 KB, so bob blocked in write(2), never exited, and the call hung until the 20s defaultTimeout threw timedOut. Fix (bob-mac-capture 8b40e08): drain both pipes concurrently on background readers from launch (DispatchGroup entered before launch), resume only after exit + both EOFs, timeout covering the whole span. Real-vault harness on mac (final run): `:` -> task_link 591 candidates in 0.031s, index 55 sections in 0.043s, filters 6-26ms; `:gtd` -> 166 rows in 0.023s; `Buy milk\n\n:` cursor 11 -> 591 rows in 0.025s. No timedOut.

COMMITS: bob-cli 5ef8eb7, d67bbb0, b672114, 8f2a02e (no bob-cli code change needed in this tale). bob-mac-capture e9865e6, 6191dec, plus this tale: 8b40e08 (concurrent drain + vault-sized regression tests + chip-refetch fix + Text deprecation cleanup), e7cb242 (15 panel tests + 6 real-bob fixtures), 9de8eb9 (:dee partial-presentation correction).

RESULTS: macOS 26 SwiftPM run 36770569427 fully green (Lint, Build, Test, Bundle, Verify plist/signature, Launch smoke, Install/reinstall). Chip-refetch fix: openPickerFromChip presents from chip candidates on bare `:` (cursor == r.start+1), refetching only when a query was typed. Tests: 1MiB/256KiB drain test, 600-row decode test, 600-row end-to-end picker test, batch open at {10,11}, selection chip, filter keystrokes run no subprocess, single completion for bare `:`, fast-typed `:dee` partial-after-refetch, Return/= /Shift-Return/Command-Return submit (recorded capture argv asserted), Backspace empties, two-stage Escape, ID-less prefill/splice/=/submit/duplicate-error. Fixtures (all real-bob output on the worked-example vault, BOB_NOW 2026-09-30 09:02:00, sanity-checked identical to task-link-complete-full.json): task-link-parse-buymilk, task-link-complete-buymilk, task-link-task-id-success, task-link-task-id-duplicate (exit 1), task-link-capture-deep-fix, task-link-capture-fix-flaky-gkeep. Text+Text deprecation warnings gone (mac build prints none from either file). One red CI along the way (36770217719): my :dee test wrongly mirrored the `^` full-snapshot flow; real bob answers `:dee` with {0,4} so the {0,1} refetch can't match — corrected the test to the actual partial presentation in 9de8eb9, then green.

notes.author: bob-cli-j.land
notes.text: RELATED: bob-cli-j.1 — the capture-grammar refactor moved POMODORO_BLOCK_ID_ERROR into src/native/capture_language.rs:625 (it was in capture.rs before), so the fix belongs there now. The string is also surfaced through 'bob capture-parse' diagnostics (code invalid_pomodoro_block_id), not just 'bob capture' execution errors, so update any test asserting either path.

plus_one_evidence.note: Reproduced on master 1e4b2ee (2026-08-14), a tree that contains this bead's 2026-08-01 close. The close fixed only one of the two strings: SUB_BULLET_BLOCK_ID_ERROR (src/native/capture_language.rs:621) correctly reads "A-Z, a-z, 0-9 or '-'", but POMODORO_BLOCK_ID_ERROR (src/native/capture_language.rs:625) still reads "...A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '_' or '-'" — the exact string this bead's title names. is_block_id_byte (src/native/collect_done.rs:2345) is byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || byte == b'-', so '_' is rejected. Live repro: bob capture-parse -f json -- 'x @dev:foo_bar' emits diagnostic invalid_pomodoro_block_id with the message claiming '_' is legal. Route messages are correct and must stay as-is: is_route_token (capture_language.rs:612) does allow '_' (e.g. route gtd_daily parses cleanly). title: Priority bullet property that rolls a scheduled date
description: The Ctrl+Shift+P bullet-property picker offers a `priority` property whose P2/P3/P4 levels each write a random `scheduled` date drawn from a per-level day range configured in bob/config.yml, and the `scheduled` date picker offers a visually distinct re-rollable date suggestion whenever the current task already has a priority.

notes.author: bob-cli-e.land
notes.text:
Land verification. Read every child note and the epic's commits in both repos, then the source: config validation (levels label/value uniqueness, bracket/'::'/newline rejection, non-negative integer day ranges, min<=max, 'levels' rejected on non-priority entries, cross-entry 'schedules' must name another date property) in validateBulletPropertyConfig/normalizeBulletPriorityProperty; rollPriorityScheduledDate inclusive with a clamp for random()===1; priority value rows in config order with label/value/window/searchText/current; signal-high chrome, 'Filter priorities', 'priority levels', level-aware subtitles and currentLabel resolved through levelsByValue; setInlineBulletPropertyValues extracted and reused by setBulletPropertyValue with Blocked/recovery intact; ^prj routing that writes priority inline and the rolled date to frontmatter under one notice; counted 'set-priority' with a per-target roll map, per-target Blocked/recovery, project-frontmatter branch and stale-session guard; pinned dices-icon priority-roll item with Ctrl+R re-roll, footer hint only when a roll exists, and counted common-priority gating; styles, manifest 1.14.x, README row, docs/projects.md. Verified chezmoi source and deployed ~/.config/bob/config.yml carry the priority entry and match, and the vault plugin files are byte-identical to source (cmp).

Integration: no commits landed in bob-cli or bob-plugins after this epic's first commit (2026-08-03 04:15), and none landed concurrently (last non-epic commits 2026-08-01 and 2026-07-31). Both repos are on master with no other branches or PRs, so there was nothing to re-integrate. Checked adjacent pre-existing surfaces for conflict or duplication: the legacy numeric [p:: N] project/highlights field uses a distinct key and does not collide with [priority:: ...]; bob-cli's Rust Tasks parser already accepts the written values; README.md, docs/dataview.md and docs/task-status-hooks.md do not enumerate picker properties, so nothing went stale.

Defect found and fixed as epic work (bob-plugins ed6386f, navigation-hotkeys 1.14.1): the single-task writer upserted priority and then scheduled onto the live line, so a task that already carried [scheduled:: ...] had that field replaced in place and ended with [priority:: ...] rightmost - the opposite of the counted writer, which rebuilds the date after the priority. Harmless while every level value is a Tasks priority name, but the plan documents changing 'value:' in config as the supported way to store a literal P2, and under that config the old order would have hidden scheduled/id/dependsOn from every right-to-left trailing-field parse. Inline writes now accept reorderPropertyNames and drop the schedules field before writing the priority; both writers assert the exact resulting line shape. npm test 268/268, npm run validate 6/6, git diff --check clean, re-synced to the vault and re-verified byte parity.

No PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP entries were recorded on any child bead, so no task beads were proposed. 'just symvision' is not available in this project (no recipe in the justfile, no symvision binary), so no epic-symbol whitelist sweep was possible; no whitelist entries naming this epic exist in the repo. Obsidian plugin reload is still required to pick up 1.14.1.

title: bob-navigation-hotkeys: plain scheduled-property picker write doesn't thread picker baseDate as today for Blocked marking
close_reason: Let's let this slide for now.
description:
In BulletPropertyPickerModal.applySelectedValue (plugins/bob-navigation-hotkeys/main.js, bob-plugins repo), the generic (non-priority, non-project-frontmatter) branch calls this.plugin.setBulletPropertyValue(...) without a `today` option:

    return await this.plugin.setBulletPropertyValue(
      this.editor,
      this.cursor,
      this.selectedPropertyItem.property.name,
      item.value,
      {
        filePath: this.filePath,
        expectedLine: this.lineText,
        scheduleLog: options.scheduleLog,
      },
    );

setBulletPropertyValue forwards to setInlineBulletPropertyValues, whose blocking check falls back to `options.today instanceof Date ? ... : new Date()` -- i.e. real wall-clock time -- when deciding whether a chosen `scheduled` date is "future" and should mark the task Blocked ([?]).

This is inconsistent with the priority-level write path (setBulletPriorityValue), which explicitly threads `baseDate: this.valueBaseDate` through as `today` so Blocked-marking is reproducible relative to the picker's own fixed base date, not the real clock.

Effect: picking a plain scheduled date (including the pinned priority-roll suggestion row in the `scheduled` value stage, which also goes through this generic branch) produces Blocked-marking that silently depends on when the code actually runs, not on the picker's `valueBaseDate`. A fixture asserting a specific Blocked/[?'] vs unblocked/[ ] outcome for this path will start failing (or silently stop covering the intended case) as real time passes the fixture's hardcoded dates.

Found while implementing bob-cli's plan sase/repos/plans/202608/auto_schedule_reasons.md (deterministic schedule-log reasons for machine-rolled dates). A new test for the pinned priority-roll suggestion ("choosing a priority roll writes immediately with a deterministic reason instead of prompting", scripts/test-navigation-hotkeys.cjs) had to read the actual checkbox status at runtime via helpers.getObsidianTaskCheckboxStatus() instead of asserting a hardcoded [?'] or [ ], specifically to route around this wall-clock dependency -- the plan's own worked example assumed [?'] but the assertion only holds if the test happens to run before the rolled date, which is not guaranteed.

Suggested fix: thread `today: this.valueBaseDate` (falling back to a fresh Date the way the priority path already does) through applySelectedValue's generic property branch, matching the priority branch's existing pattern.

title: Clear the retired agent-hood publication requests blocking commit-link publication
description:
sase agent sync reports publication requests that were retired as unpublishable and never cleared, and the retirement now degrades commit traceability: every sase_git_commit into bobs-org/bob-mac-capture warns 'this project already has 2 retired agent-hood publication requests. The link written to this commit may remain unavailable until the outbox is cleared.' The SASE_AGENT link in those commit messages therefore points at an agent page that may never materialize.

Not specific to one project. sase agent sync --check --json also shows the same class of quarantine diagnostic under project actstat: "publication request bbugyi200.athena.sase-js.9@9f51c7b86c58 retired as unpublishable: published agent page for 'bbugyi200.athena.sase-js.9' did not materialize during full sync; run 'sase agent sync --drop-retired' to drop it".

The tool names its own remedy: sase agent sync --drop-retired, which drops retired publication requests and reports how many were dropped and why. Scope: run it, confirm the outbox clears for every affected project, re-run a commit (or sase agent sync --check) to confirm the warning is gone, and confirm whether the affected commits' SASE_AGENT links now resolve or need a republish. Left unrun by agents so far because the flagless sync also drains publication retries, publishes commit-eligible hoods, and pushes across projects — a cross-cutting action outside any one phase's scope.

Proposed as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note by epic phase bead bob-cli-j.4, and re-observed by the bob-cli-j land agent on commit f59ab74.
